summary: Oranjemund Airport (OMD) serves the remote diamond mining town of Oranjemund in southernmost Namibia, near the Orange River border with South Africa. The airport primarily supports Namdeb diamond mining operations and a small number of scheduled flights linking the town to Windhoek. Once part of the highly restricted Sperrgebiet diamond zone, the surrounding region has become more accessible to visitors since its designation as the Tsau //Khaeb National Park.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines fly to Oranjemund Airport?
A: Scheduled service is typically provided by small regional carriers connecting Oranjemund with Windhoek's Eros Airport on a limited basis.

Q: How far is the airport from Oranjemund town?
A: The airport is located just a few kilometres outside the town centre, making transfers quick and straightforward.

Q: Is Oranjemund open to tourists?
A: Access has expanded significantly in recent years since parts of the former Sperrgebiet diamond area were opened as Tsau //Khaeb National Park, though some permits and arrangements are still required.

Q: Can I cross into South Africa from Oranjemund?
A: Yes, the Orange River border crossing to Alexander Bay in South Africa is nearby, though operating hours should be confirmed before travel.
transport_tips: Rental cars and pre-arranged hotel transfers are the most reliable ways to reach the town, as public transport options in this remote area are very limited. Flights are infrequent and weather in the coastal Namib desert can occasionally cause delays, so building in buffer time is wise. The drive from Springbok in South Africa takes roughly four to five hours via the border crossing if arriving overland.
